title: Annotatio IV §.II: John 6 = antecedent most lucid commentary on the Institution words
pass_a_gloss: Moreover in this latter way John 6 treats so specially of the Sacred Supper and of the sacramental presence and participation of Christ’s flesh and blood, that what this sacramental Mode of either is, and of what sort it is to be judged, is there set out most expressly of all; wherefore we judge Christ’s discourse held in John 6 to be the antecedent and most lucid Commentary on Christ’s Institution words — i.e. a Commentary not on the Supper already then instituted, but on the Sacred Supper shortly to be instituted, holding so great a torch to it, and lending so much light to the concise Institution words This is my Body, and For this is my blood, that Christ’s disciples, fully freed from all their objections and doubts by that discourse of their Master, those words either moved or could move no further scruple.
pass_b_english: So read, John 6 specially exposes what the sacramental Mode of presence and participation is — the antecedent, most lucid commentary on the Institution words.
Not on a Supper already instituted then, but on the one soon to be: torch and light for ‘This is my Body’ / ‘This is my blood,’ clearing the disciples’ scruples.
source_text: Ceterum hôc posteriori modo cap. Joh. 6. de S. Cœna deque Sacramentali & carnis & sanguinis Christi tùm præsentia, tùm participatione, ita specialtim agitur, ut quis hic modus sacramentalis utriusque, & qualis censendus sit, omnium disertissimè inibi exponatur, quô proinde nomine sermonem Christi, Joh. 6. cap. habitum, antecedaneum verborum Institutionis Christi eumque luculentissimum Commentarium arbitramur esse, i. e. Commentarium non de jam tum instituta, sed de paulò post instituenda S. Cœna, tantam huic facem præferentem, tantumque luminis, concisis Institutionis Christi verbis: Hoc est Corpus meum, & Hic enim sanguis meus, fæneratum, ut Discipulis Christi, per Magistri sui sermonem istum, objectionibus & dubiis suis omnibus plenissimè liberatis, nullum amplius scrupulum ista vel moverint, vel quiverint movere.
